paragraphs: Friend, here's the lesson that hits hardest, and I'm going to say it plain. The writer tells us why all this happened: "because of the anger of the LORD, all this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until He finally banished them from His presence" (2 Kings 24:20). Zedekiah did evil, just as Jehoiakim had done (2 Kings 24:19), and he rebelled against the king who put him on the throne. Sin that keeps getting waved off doesn't stay small, and this passage shows where that road ends.

I think this one is heavy, so I'm not going to joke my way past it. The city fell, the temple that Solomon built burned, and Judah was taken into exile, away from its own land (2 Kings 25:9, 21). Zedekiah had a crown, an army and a whole city behind him, and none of it held when he kept going his own way. Nothing you lean on besides God can carry that weight, whether it's a title, a paycheck or a plan that looks airtight.

But hold on, baker, because the writer doesn't pretend the story is finished. Judah is far from home, yet the LORD hasn't stopped being the LORD. A hard ending like this is a warning, and it's also a reason to listen the first time, so you don't have to learn it the hard way. Take it seriously, keep your ovens ready, and stay close, because this story still has pages left.
